summary: Reviewed FR-001–FR-017, SC-001–SC-005, scenarios, edge cases, tasks, accepted test seams and commit proofs. Resolver/CLI paths, parity, refusal and declared injected-failure tests are present; FR-003, FR-005/009 and FR-006/SC-001 have runtime integration gaps, and FR-013/014 have init failure/race gaps. Targeted model tests pass (9 tests).

findings.summary: Resolved models cannot be persisted or updated through the state writer
findings.evidence: FR-005 and FR-009 require recording resolved values and sources and updating them on resume; T007/T009 are checked. SKILL.md:47 only instructs recording/overwriting the block, while references/state.md:170 makes the CLI the sole writer and forbids hand edits. The new cli.py:130-153 only exposes read-only models and project init; no state operation accepts models, and commands.py:1499-1529 cmd_resume changes only status/history. Therefore neither pending nor resumed run can satisfy the required state/delta contract. ENG-15, ENG-26.
findings.fix: Add a validated single-writer operation that persists resolved models for pending and worktree runs, returns prior/current deltas, and invoke it in preflight and resume.

findings.summary: Installed orchestrator has no role-to-tier mapping for model selection
findings.evidence: FR-006 and SC-001 require every spawn to receive the model for its role's tier. SKILL.md:24 refers to the tier but provides no mapping. Authored tiers exist in core/roles/*.md frontmatter (for example spec-builder is deep and code-build is standard); tools/render.py:196-200,241-242 strips that frontmatter when installing role bodies, and agent_fields at 124-162 writes the selected model but not its tier. The installed skill therefore cannot reliably determine which resolved value to pass, especially when both tiers previously used the same model. T007/T008 are checked but do not supply this prerequisite.
findings.fix: Ship an authoritative role-to-tier mapping accessible to the installed orchestrator and use it for each spawn; validate it against authored roles.

findings.summary: Omitting a spawn model does not clear a pinned installed agent model
findings.evidence: FR-003 and US1 scenario 4 require an empty winning value to inherit the session's model without reinstalling. adapters/opencode/harness.md:15 and adapters/claude-code/harness.md:14-15 instead omit the tool model parameter. Existing rendered custom agents retain their own nonempty model: tools/render.py:159-161 writes adapter/user selections into each role's agent frontmatter, including default OpenCode and Claude Code selections. Omitting a call override leaves that agent selection in effect rather than clearing it to the session model, so a project empty-string override can silently use the old installed selection.
findings.fix: Implement a harness-supported way to explicitly select the invoking session model when the resolved value is empty, without relying on omission of a parameter on a model-pinned agent; verify both supported adapters.

findings.summary: Concurrent init can overwrite a newly created project config
findings.evidence: FR-014 requires init to refuse an existing config and modify nothing; FR-015 and the plan state no clobber. models.py:90 checks existence before resolving and staging, but line 119 publishes with os.replace, which overwrites any config another init or user creates between the check and replace. ENG-26.
findings.fix: Publish the staged config using atomic no-replace semantics or an appropriate exclusive protocol, and refuse a competing creation.

findings.summary: README publication failure leaves init incomplete and impossible to retry
findings.evidence: FR-011 and FR-013 require init to create both config and sidecar; models.py:108-119 publishes config before attempting README. If config.README.md is a directory or its replacement fails, init exits with an uncaught exception after creating config.json; the next attempt hits the refusal at line 90, so it cannot finish the required README without manual removal. ENG-17 and ENG-26.
findings.fix: Stage both files and make failure recoverable without deleting or overwriting an independently created configuration; surface a clear error.
